287124783_6e2163da.text: "PVNCRH neurons are classically regarded as the neuroendocrine entry point for driving glucocorticoid secretion. However, accumulating evidence indicates that, beyond this endocrine role, they also use fast transmitters and CRH co-transmission to form functional projections to diverse brain regions and pre-sympathetic circuits, thereby regulating stress dimensions that extend beyond HPA axis output, including defensive behaviors, reward and motivation, arousal-sleep regulation, autonomic output and glucose homeostasis."
